name: EFM32ZG110F32-B-QFN24R
title: EFM32 Zero Gecko: 32-bit ARM Cortex-M0+ microcontrollers, 24 MHz, up to 32 kB flash, AES, 12-bit ADC, QFN24, QFN32 and TQFP48
summary: A family of very low-power 32-bit microcontrollers on the ARM Cortex-M0+ core at up to 24 MHz, carrying 4 to 32 kB of flash and 2 or 4 kB of RAM. They draw 114 µA/MHz running from flash, 0.9 µA in Deep Sleep with the RTC on, and 20 nA in Shutoff, and wake from Stop in 2 µs. Peripherals include a USART, a low-energy UART, I2C, two 16-bit timers, an RTC, a pulse counter, a 4-channel DMA, hardware AES, a 12-bit 1 Msps ADC, a current DAC and an analog comparator with capacitive sensing. EFM32ZG110F32-B-QFN24 is the 32 kB flash, 4 kB RAM part in QFN24 with 17 GPIO.
key_figures: 32/16/8/4 kB flash; 4 kB RAM (32 and 16 kB parts), 2 kB (8 and 4 kB parts)
114 µA/MHz typ (EM0, 21 MHz HFRCO, from flash, 3 V)
48 µA/MHz EM1; 0.9 µA EM2; 0.5 µA EM3; 0.02 µA EM4 (typ, 3 V, 25 °C)
12-bit, 1 Msps; 2 inputs on ZG110, 4 on ZG210 and ZG222; none on ZG108
USART, LEUART, I2C, 2 × 16-bit TIMER, 24-bit RTC, PCNT, ACMP, VCMP, IDAC, AES, 4-ch DMA, 4-ch PRS
QFN24 5 × 5 mm, QFN32 6 × 6 mm, TQFP48 7 × 7 mm

operation.text: The EFM32 Zero Gecko (ZG) parts differ by package, pin count and analog content. EFM32ZG108 and EFM32ZG110 are QFN24 parts with 17 GPIO; the ZG108 has no ADC, IDAC or AES. EFM32ZG210 is QFN32 with 24 GPIO, EFM32ZG222 is TQFP48 with 37 GPIO and five ACMP inputs. Each comes with 4, 8, 16 or 32 kB of flash; the 4 and 8 kB parts have 2 kB of RAM, the 16 and 32 kB parts 4 kB. All run up to 24 MHz from 1.98 V to 3.8 V over -40 to 85 °C.

An ordering code reads, left to right: EFM32 (32-bit energy friendly MCU), ZG (Zero Gecko), a feature-set code (108, 110, 210, 222), F (flash memory), the flash size in kB, the revision letter (B), the package (QFN or QFP), the pin count, and an optional T for tray.
ARM Cortex-M0+ at up to 24 MHz, up to 0.9 Dhrystone MIPS/MHz, with a wake-up interrupt controller that handles interrupts raised while the CPU sleeps, and a SysTick timer.
Two-pin Serial Wire debug. SWCLK (PF0, internal pull-down) and SWDIO (PF1, internal pull-up) are on their pins from reset.

The MSC owns the flash, which both the CPU and the DMA can read and write. The flash has a main block for program code and an information block for user data and lock bits, holding also a read-only page of system and calibration data. Flash read and write work in EM0 and EM1.
A 4-channel DMA controller (ARM PL230 µDMA) moves data without the CPU, for example from the USART to RAM, so the part can stay in a low-energy mode while data moves.

Five energy modes, managed by the EMU. EM0 Active and EM1 Sleep are the two running modes; EM1 draws 48 µA/MHz typ and EM0 114 µA/MHz typ at 3 V. EM2 Deep Sleep: the RTC with its 32.768 kHz oscillator and the LEUART with the DMA keep working; RAM and CPU state, power-on reset and brown-out detector kept. EM3 Stop: RAM and CPU state, power-on reset and brown-out detector kept; I2C address recognition and the pulse counter still work. EM4 Shutoff: pin output states are kept, and the GPIO_EM4WU pins wake the part. The EMU can also turn off power to unused SRAM blocks.

After a power-on, brown-out or pin reset is released, program execution starts 163 µs typ later. The brown-out detector trips at 1.74 V to 1.96 V on a falling supply and releases near 1.85 V on a rising one. RESETn has an internal pull-up; an external reset source should only pull it low.

AVDD_x, VDD_DREG and IOVDD_x must all be joined on the board, with an optional filter between them. DECOUPLE is the internal regulator's output and needs CDECOUPLE, 1 µF typ (X5R recommended), to ground. Board guidance is in application note AN0002.

Six oscillators: a 4 to 24 MHz crystal oscillator (HFXO), an RC oscillator with bands near 1.2, 6.6, 11, 14 and 21 MHz (HFRCO), an auxiliary RC oscillator with the same bands (AUXHFRCO), a 32.768 kHz crystal oscillator (LFXO), a 32.768 kHz RC oscillator (LFRCO) and an ultra-low-frequency RC oscillator of 0.7 to 1.75 kHz (ULFRCO). The CMU enables and configures each oscillator and turns the clock of each peripheral on or off on its own. HFXTAL_N and LFXTAL_N also take an external clock. Crystal load and start-up settings for the LFXO are covered by application note AN0016.
The watchdog generates a reset on a system failure, such as one caused by software or by an outside event like an ESD pulse. It runs from its own RC oscillator at about 50 nA.
Four PRS channels carry signals from producer peripherals straight to consumer peripherals without the CPU; edge detection can be applied on the way. A pin's input can be routed through the PRS too.

One I2C interface, master or slave, multi-master capable, at Standard, Fast and Fast-mode Plus speeds from 10 kbit/s up to 1 Mbit/s. It handles arbitration and bus timeouts on the slave side, as SMBus needs. Slave address recognition works in all energy modes.
USART1 runs full-duplex asynchronous UART, RS-485, SPI, MicroWire and 3-wire, and talks to ISO 7816 smart cards, IrDA and I2S devices; it is triple buffered and supports half duplex.
Every part leaves the factory with a UART bootloader (application note AN0003) on BOOT_TX (PF0) and BOOT_RX (PF1). It detects the baud rate automatically and supports destructive write.
LEUART0 runs two-way UART at up to 9600 baud from a 32.768 kHz clock alone, and with the DMA keeps working in EM2.
Two 16-bit timers, each with three channels that capture inputs or compare to drive outputs and PWM.
A 24-bit real-time counter clocked by the 32.768 kHz crystal or RC oscillator; it runs in EM0, EM1 and EM2.
PCNT0 has a 16-bit count register and counts pulses on one input or decodes quadrature inputs. It is clocked from LFACLK or from its PCNT0_S0IN pin and works in EM0 to EM3.

ACMP0 compares two inputs, either pins or internal references, and gives a digital output. Its bias current sets both response time and current draw. It does capacitive sensing on up to 5 inputs, with a selectable internal resistor of 39 to 136 kΩ.
VCMP watches the supply and raises an interrupt when it crosses a programmable level, VDD trigger level = 1.667 V + 0.034 × TRIGLEVEL. Its bias sets response time and current.

A 12-bit SAR ADC at up to 1 Msamples/s. Its input mux takes 4 external pins and 6 internal signals, single-ended or as 2 differential pairs, and includes the on-chip temperature sensor. References: internal 1.25 V and 2.5 V, VDD, 5 V differential, 2xVDD, or an external reference on channels 6 and 7.
The current DAC sources or sinks a programmable constant current, 0.05 µA to 64 µA in four ranges, out of a pin (IDAC0_OUT) or to the ADC.

Hardware AES encrypts and decrypts with 128-bit keys; one 128-bit block takes 52 HFCORECLK cycles. It sits on the AHB, and every write to it must be a 32-bit access; 8-bit and 16-bit writes are not supported.

Up to 37 GPIO in ports of up to 16 pins. Each pin is set on its own as input or output, push-pull or open-drain, with pull-up or pull-down, input filter and drive strength (DRIVEMODE LOWEST, LOW, STANDARD, HIGH). Peripheral signals override the GPIO and can be routed to several locations. Up to 16 asynchronous external interrupts reach any pin.

A peripheral signal written NAME #n can be placed at location n; a pin carrying several locations of one signal lists them as #a/b. The location is chosen with the LOCATION bitfield of the module's *_ROUTE register.

Typical figures are at TAMB = 25 °C and VDD = 3.0 V. Min and max figures cover the worst case of ambient temperature, supply voltage and frequency within the general operating conditions, unless a row says otherwise.

The top marking carries an orientation mark, the EFM32 family mark, a chip-version line followed by a temperature-grade letter, a two-line production code, and the revision letter, which gives the chip revision.
Pb-free reflow per the current IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020; the peak soldering temperature is 260 °C.
